newsitem.title: USA: USWC crudes extend gains, with heavy deals done.
newsitem.headline: USWC crudes extend gains, with heavy deals done.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices extended yesterday's gains at midday, tracking a futures market which rose after data released on Tuesday showed tight heating oil inventories.
NYMEX October crude oil rose 56 cents in late trade, reaching $23.87 a barrel.
But crude followed cues from heating oil, which jumped 2.21 cents a gallon to 67.80 cents for October deliveries.
Prices for California Kern River crude rose 20 to 30 cents to $15.90/16.10 a barrel after traders quoted offers at higher levels.
"It's definitely not as weak as it was a couple weeks ago," one trader said, noting last week's 15,000 barrel purchase by Shell Oil.
Discounts for lighter grade Alaska North Slope remained at $2.30 under WTI, the level of last week's deal.
Outright prices for the grade rose to $21.15/21.45 a barrel.
A trader for one major refinery said spot deals for foreign cargoes had turned scarce after ANS prices fell in recent weeks.
"With ANS at $2.30 it's tough to get foreign barrels to compete," he said.
A large volume of Line 63 grade was bought by a major West Coast refiner at posting plus $1.00, lower than its previous level of $1.05. Supplies remained adequate, traders said.
Deltas for fixed deals of Line 63 remained $3.20/3.00 a barrel under WTI, after widening last week.
Values for lightly traded Wilmington grade held at $17.40/17.50.
